forces.title: AI-driven environments consolidate consumer attention and traffic
forces.description: Consumer discovery is increasingly shifting from the open web to AI-driven environments. Over 50% of Google searches now include AI-generated overviews, risking 20-50% of traditional open-web search traffic by 2030. AI ranking also shapes over 50% of Instagram content and 95% of TikTok watch time. This means brand visibility depends heavily on a few AI systems, creating a major structural shift for Search, Social & Content Platforms.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI agents increasingly mediate advertiser and consumer decisions
forces.description: AI is increasingly mediating purchasing decisions, with more than 90% of advertisers using AI for media planning, budgeting, targeting, and creative generation. On the consumer side, shopping agents and AI assistants rank products, compare alternatives, and complete transactions, with some early deployments showing up to 60% higher conversion rates. This fundamental shift towards agentic purchasing influences 10-35% of e-commerce transactions, creating a critical structural change for platforms.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Value concentrating in platforms bundling data, measurement, and transactions
forces.description: As attention, decision-making, buying, conversion, and measurement converge into integrated AI-driven environments, value is increasingly concentrating among AI-native platforms and walled gardens that offer these bundled capabilities. This shifts value away from traditional intermediaries (exchanges, ad networks, agencies). Advertisers risk losing visibility and control over ad placements due to reliance on 'black box optimization' systems, making measurement more opaque and concentrating power within these dominant platforms.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI drives increased total advertising spend and return on ad spend
forces.description: AI is projected to expand total advertising spend, with nearly three-quarters of surveyed companies expecting an increase in the next 12 months. This growth is fueled by new use cases like AI shopping agents and AI-enabled improvements in Return on Ad Spend (ROAS). One-third of advertisers believe ROAS will increase by more than 10% due to AI. This represents a significant tailwind for Search, Social & Content Platforms that can leverage AI effectively.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad tech intermediaries face compression from AI buying agents
forces.description: The ad tech 'middle' is compressing as AI-native buying agents can replicate cross-platform optimization within a single workflow. This could eliminate key use cases for supply-side platforms, exchanges, traditional demand-side platforms, and undifferentiated middleware. With 82% of advertisers planning direct AI ad format purchases, intermediation layers built on cross-platform arbitrage will play a smaller role, posing a significant headwind for traditional ad tech players.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Declining open web traffic challenges publishers, requiring new strategies
forces.description: With traditional search traffic declining and consumers embracing AI-generated answers, AI accelerates the eroding economics of the open web. Click-driven, scale-dependent publishing becomes less viable, impacting long-tail, SEO-dependent sites without user subscription models. Publishers must consider content licensing to AI platforms for training data and developing Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) capabilities to maintain visibility in AI answers, or forming premium audience coalitions.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Walled gardens expand automation to commerce and agent offerings
forces.description: Established walled gardens are strategically extending their automation beyond media monetization into commerce and AI agent offerings. Examples include TikTok's projected $30 billion in commerce GMV by 2028 and Meta's integration of AI agents across its apps. These aggressive expansions will allow these platforms to increasingly control the entire customer journey, from discovery to transaction, setting new terms for competitive advantage in the advertising ecosystem.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI-native platforms exploring new monetization models
forces.description: AI-native platforms like OpenAI are experimenting with sponsored recommendations, commerce integrations, and proprietary transaction flows to monetize their rapidly expanding share of consumer discovery. Their focus on monetizing high-intent user interactions suggests a move towards a more direct role in commercial journeys, potentially allowing them to control discovery, purchase, and measurement more completely. This creates significant new revenue opportunities for these platforms.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Generative AI necessitates shift from SEO to GEO for online visibility
forces.description: The rise of agentic AI and generative AI models is ending traditional internet search. Businesses now need to invest in Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to be recognized by AI systems that understand user preferences. This requires rethinking how online information is categorized, using clear, structured data readable by AI. Content creators have a significant opportunity to become experts in optimizing client brands for discovery in this new AI-driven era, impacting all platforms relying on content discovery.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Media content creators gain opportunity in AI content optimization
forces.description: The generational shift towards agentic AI and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) presents a significant opportunity for media content creators. With AI models increasingly displacing traditional internet search, these creators can become experts in optimizing content to ensure client brands are discovered in the new AI economy. This involves structuring data clearly, providing value directly, and answering user queries efficiently for AI tools, transforming how brand visibility is achieved on digital platforms.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Generative AI projected to capture 10% of search market by 2026
forces.description: Generative AI models are rapidly increasing their share of the overall search market, projected to reach 10% by 2026. This growth signifies a fundamental shift in how users seek and receive information, with AI tools becoming a primary method. This trend directly impacts traditional search engines and content platforms, compelling them to adapt their optimization strategies (GEO) to remain relevant in an evolving AI-driven discovery landscape.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Digital video advertising fueled by AI hyper-personalization and mobile
forces.description: Digital video advertising (DVA) in Ireland is projected for rapid expansion, driven by increasing internet penetration, AI-enabled hyper-personalization, and targeted advertising. Mobile devices are expected to account for 80.3% of total DVA spending by 2030, indicating a strong shift in consumption patterns. Businesses across all sectors are utilizing DVA, transforming their marketing strategies and creating significant growth opportunities for ad-driven content platforms.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Agentic AI transforms routine tasks with autonomous decision-making
forces.description: Agentic AI, building on large language models, enables AI agents to understand complex text and context, produce nuanced human-quality outputs, and act autonomously to optimize, automate, and execute routine tasks. These systems can assess situations, make plans, and take actions with minimal human intervention, effectively performing "digital labor." This next-generation AI, exemplified by agents booking travel based on preferences, offers infinite potential uses and significant efficiency benefits across various industries, including Search, Social & Content Platforms.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: GenAI faces reproducibility, explainability, and data quality challenges
forces.description: Despite rapid advancements, the actual business impact of Generative AI (GenAI) on revenue and operations remains limited for many enterprises, with issues such as reproducibility (consistent results), explainability (understanding decision-making), and data quality posing significant challenges. The effectiveness of AI systems is heavily dependent on robust data governance, risk management, and ethical frameworks. Without proper oversight, AI systems could amplify biases and make opaque decisions, presenting a key risk to its widespread and effective deployment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Direct media deals bypass agencies, favoring platforms
forces.description: A growing share of media spend, currently roughly half, is flowing through direct channels, bypassing traditional advertising agencies. This trend is accelerated by AI, which can dramatically disrupt core agency activities such as planning, buying, and creative production. For Search, Social & Content Platforms, this means increased direct engagement with advertisers, potentially leading to greater control over ad inventory and stronger revenue streams, while posing a headwind for agencies.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI-generated overviews threaten traditional open-web search traffic
forces.description: AI-generated overviews are becoming a prominent feature in Google searches, with over 50% of searches now including them. This development poses a significant risk to traditional open-web search, as 20% to 50% of its traffic could be jeopardized by 2030. For search engine platforms (a core component of IN090301), this shift means a potential reduction in user engagement with traditional search results, necessitating adaptation to retain user attention and advertising value in an AI-dominated search landscape.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: AI to drive growth and significant discontinuity in advertising
viewpoints.description: AI is rapidly adopted by consumers and businesses, acting as a growth engine and accelerating existing tectonic shifts in advertising. While three-quarters of advertisers expect increased media spend, and one-third foresee over 10% ROAS increase, the shift away from the open web and towards direct media deals will cause discontinuity. Value will move to players who can shape what consumers see, select, and purchase. This suggests a transformative but challenging period for Search, Social & Content Platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Walled gardens well-positioned to expand into commerce and AI agents
viewpoints.description: Established walled gardens (e.g., TikTok, YouTube, Meta) are well-positioned for the new AI-driven advertising era. They are strategically moving beyond just monetizing attention to integrate commerce and agent offerings, aiming to control discovery, purchase, and measurement more directly. This expansion, exemplified by TikTok's commerce growth and Meta's AI agent integration, will allow them to shape the terms for other players in the advertising ecosystem.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: AI-native platforms poised to develop strong advertising models
viewpoints.description: AI-native platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) hold a rapidly expanding share of consumer discovery for product research due to their conversational interfaces and agent layers. They possess inherent advantages of privileged access to the decision moment and significant behavioral data, but currently lack a mature advertising model. These platforms are experimenting with sponsored answers, commerce integrations, and proprietary transaction flows, potentially controlling discovery, purchase, and measurement directly.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Ireland's AI adoption surpasses EU average, moving to execution
viewpoints.description: Artificial intelligence tools are now firmly embedded across Irish workplaces, with 43% of private-sector organizations and 36% of public-sector bodies actively using AI. This adoption rate exceeds the EU average and is consistent across all organization sizes and sectors. The trend indicates a shift from planning to active deployment of AI, underscoring its growing importance in the Irish economy and its impact on various industries including Search, Social & Content Platforms.
viewpoints.source_firm: Trinity College, Dublin (as cited by Bank of Ireland)
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: AI concentrates advertising power in walled gardens and native platforms
viewpoints.description: As AI becomes deeply embedded in media buying, the advertising landscape is undergoing a transformation towards greater automation, integration, and concentration. This shift is channeling power and value towards a smaller number of dominant walled gardens and AI-native platforms. These platforms, including search engines and social media, will increasingly shape discovery, recommendation, and transactions, compelling other players to adapt to rules set by these AI-driven giants.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: AI environments consolidate consumer attention, benefiting platforms
viewpoints.description: Consumer discovery is increasingly moving into AI-driven environments, with over 50% of Google searches featuring AI overviews and the majority of content on platforms like Instagram and TikTok being algorithmically generated. This consolidation of attention reinforces the central role of Search, Social & Content Platforms that leverage AI, as brand visibility becomes highly dependent on these few AI systems. This trend represents a strong positive for platforms positioned at the forefront of AI integration.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: AI agents enhance purchasing, increasing platform conversion rates
viewpoints.description: AI agents are increasingly mediating purchase decisions, from advertisers' media planning to consumers' shopping. Early deployments of AI-enabled shopping and recommendation experiences have shown up to 60% higher conversion rates. This trend, where 10-35% of e-commerce transactions could be AI-influenced, signifies a strong positive for Search, Social & Content Platforms that integrate AI agents. These platforms can capture more value by facilitating higher conversion, moving beyond mere attention aggregation to direct action.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Integrated platforms capture value by bundling data, measurement
viewpoints.description: Value in advertising is concentrating among AI-native platforms and walled gardens that bundle capabilities like attention, decision-making, buying, conversion, and measurement into single, AI-managed products. This integration streamlines the advertising process, providing superior closed-loop measurement and transaction visibility. For Search, Social & Content Platforms, this structural shift means they are increasingly positioned to capture a disproportionate share of advertising value by offering comprehensive, integrated solutions to advertisers.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Technology platforms outperform telecom in growth rates
viewpoints.description: Large technology platforms, including those in Search, Social & Content Platforms, are perceived to achieve significantly higher growth rates compared to the European telecom sector. This disparity is attributed to the infrastructure-like returns and regulatory frameworks that limit product differentiation, pricing, and advertising opportunities for telecom companies. This implies a more dynamic and less constrained growth environment for ad-driven internet platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: European telecoms set to see modest growth in 2026

Artificial intelligence allows for highly targeted and personalized advertising, increasing effectiveness and demand.
The ability to precisely target specific consumer segments drives higher advertiser investment.

Advertisers expect higher returns on their ad spend due to AI optimization, incentivizing further investment.

While no specific monetary value is provided, the sentiment indicates a significant expansion in the market for platforms monetized by advertising.
